title: Annotators with Attitudes: How Annotator Beliefs And Identities Bias Toxic Language Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating how annotators' racial identities (Black vs. White) and endorsement of racist beliefs (measured via the Modern Racism Scale) correlate with their toxicity and racism ratings for anti-Black hate speech and African American English (AAE) posts.

Measuring the perceived toxicity of African American English (AAE) text compared to canonical English, and correlating these ratings with annotators' language purism attitudes, race, and political leanings.

Assessing how annotators' political leanings (conservative vs. liberal) and adherence to traditionalist values or free speech attitudes influence their offensiveness and racism ratings for various text categories.
Comparing the offensiveness and racism ratings provided by male and female annotators across different types of social media posts to identify gender-based differences in toxicity perception.
